problem: Prior LLM-for-robotics work uses LLMs mainly as text-to-action translators or relies on embodied/simulation training; it is unclear whether a purely text-and-image-trained MLLM can directly pilot a real robot from first-person images and show world-model-like behavior.
motivation: Cognitive science and robotics theories claim intelligence requires a body and sensorimotor experience. If a disembodied MLLM can control a physical robot zero-shot and reason about the consequences of its own actions, this challenges that view and suggests emergent world-model-like understanding.
key_idea: Place GPT-5.1 (frozen, no embodiment training) in a closed loop as the high-level controller of a real differential-drive robot using only low-res first-person images and discrete motion commands, and qualitatively probe for signs of spatial and physical world modeling.
insight: Reasoning traces show behaviors consistent with a world model: inferring an object is off-frame to the left after advancing, and reversing after collision to visually check whether the penguin toppled. However, the evidence is qualitative and from a few trials; failures (spiral approaches, misidentifying a distant penguin, getting stuck without tactile sensing) show limits, and there is no controlled ablation separating world-model reasoning from pattern matching.
method: Closed-loop controller: at each cycle the robot camera image plus mission context is sent to GPT-5.1, which outputs a short reasoning trace and one command.
Action set: advance t seconds, reverse t seconds, or rotate by θ degrees (e.g. 2 s ≈ 40 cm); the robot's microcontroller handles low-level motor execution.
Short-term memory: all previous images and reasoning traces are accumulated in the context for the next decision.
Termination: episode ends when the model declares 'MISSION ACCOMPLISHED'.
Tasks: touch a plush penguin (including starting while facing a wall, requiring exploration), and a knock-down-the-penguin-with-the-camera task.
Evaluation: qualitative analysis of reasoning traces in three annotated runs plus small aggregate success counts (5 trials per mission).

setting.observation: monocular first-person RGB, 960×576, JPEG 85, one frame per action cycle plus history of previous frames and reasoning
setting.action_space: discrete timed primitives: advance t s, reverse t s, rotate θ degrees

numbers_note: No standard benchmark. Only informal aggregate counts in text: touch mission failed 1 of 5 trials (4/5 success); knock-down mission 2 full successes, 1 partial, 2 failures out of 5; wall-facing exploration 4 of 5 succeeded.
results: GPT-5.1 zero-shot piloted a real robot to touch a penguin (4/5 successes) and knock it down (2/5 full successes, 1 partial, 2 failures). It showed off-frame object inference and collide-reverse-verify behavior, but used inefficient spiral approaches and misidentified distant distractors. No baselines were compared.
limitations: Very small, qualitative exploratory study: one model, one robot, ~5 trials per task, no baselines or controlled ablations
Claims of a 'world model' are interpretive and not rigorously tested; alternatives such as pattern matching are not ruled out
Perceptual and control limitations: low-res images, no tactile sensing, imprecise alignment, distractor misidentification
